summary.text: Wayne Langerholc Jr. is a Republican who was first elected to the Pennsylvania Senate in November 2016 to represent the 35th District and is serving his third term as Senate Majority Whip.

paragraphs.text: Before the Senate, Langerholc was an assistant district attorney in Cambria County, an attorney in private practice, and a Richland Township supervisor. He is a graduate of Richland High School, Juniata College and Widener University Commonwealth Law School.

He previously chaired the Senate Transportation Committee and currently chairs the Aging and Youth Committee and is vice chair of Rules and Executive Nominations; he also serves on the Appropriations, Judiciary, Transportation, and Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness committees.

Bills he sponsored in the 2023-24 session that became law include a statewide rape kit evidence tracking system and authorization for farmers to deliver directly to homes. He lives in Richland Township with his wife, Cortney, and their three daughters.
